# Grounding

*Concept*

Giving an AI model content from the Search index at answer time, so that its answer rests on that content.

**Glossary** (*Grounding*): Giving an AI model content from the Google Search index at prompt time, so that its answer rests on that content.

11 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 6 shown or said at the event (3 not in Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 3 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Grounding with Google Search](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search).

- [`D2-C121`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's crawler documentation defines grounding in Gemini Apps and in Grounding with Google Search on Vertex AI as providing content from the Google Search index to the model at prompt time, and sites manage whether their content is used for it with the Google-Extended robots.txt token. `[D2-C121, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers]`
- [`D3-C094`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Docs: Google's Gemini API documentation on grounding with Google Search says the model automatically generates and runs one or more search queries when needed, and the response lists the search queries it executed. `[D3-C094, docs, Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C308`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: A community speaker said Microsoft is ahead of Google in giving site owners the grounding queries its AI uses. `[D1-C308, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C477`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: As far as the speaker knows, in most of Google's main AI uses a page's schema.org markup is not turned into text and put directly into the model's context; the data is first sorted out, checked for quality and indexed before it is passed on as grounding context. `[D2-C477, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C687`](../sessions/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Adding grounding or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on top of a model reduces hallucinations but cannot eliminate them. `[D3-C687, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C038`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: AI Mode and AI Overviews use the same crawling and the same index as Search. At serving they add grounding on the Search index and query fan-out. `[D1-C038, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C057`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's slide on how LLM features with grounding generally work showed a query going to both the search engine and an LLM, the search engine's results going to the LLM, the LLM generating fan-out queries that go back to the search engine, and the LLM returning answers with links. `[D3-C057, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C309`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker described the retrieval stage as whether an AI requests a site's pages when grounding its answer; if it does not, the cause may be a crawling or an indexing issue. `[D1-C309, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C486`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Analysis: The panel spoke of blocking Google's 'AI crawling or training' with Google-Extended, but Google documents Google-Extended as a usage token, not a crawler: disallowing it does not stop Googlebot fetching pages and only controls use for Gemini training and grounding. `[D1-C486, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C067`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: nofollow is a link-graph hint for search engines, not an access control: to keep AI crawlers away from content, use robots.txt rules for the specific crawlers; at Google, Google-Extended covers Gemini training and grounding, and the Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews and AI Mode. `[D2-C067, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C123`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Google documents Gemini grounding only as content from the Search index at prompt time; the live read of a specific page at a user's request, described on stage, is not documented, so it is unclear whether it works like a user-triggered fetcher, which generally ignores robots.txt, or follows Google-Extended. `[D2-C123, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
